## EDA

This analysis is looking at the following files:

```         
dailySteps_merged.csv
hourlyCalories_merged.csv
hourlyIntensities_merged.csv
```

The data was collected from a survey that was distributed between the dates 03.12.2016 - 05.12.2026

- Number of records and part
- Missing values
- Duplicate rows
- Date/time coverage
- Distribution of key measures
- Outliers/anomalies
- Potential joins to other datasets
- Interesting patterns and visualisations
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(plotly)
```

```{r load-data}
daily_steps <- read.csv("../data/dailySteps_merged.csv")
hourly_calories <- read.csv("../data/hourlyCalories_merged.csv")
hourly_intensities <- read.csv("../data/hourlyIntensities_merged.csv")
```
### `dailySteps_merged.csv`
- `Id`, `ActivityDay`, `StepTotal`
- Daily activity levels, patterns, differences and similarities between participants

### `hourlyCalories_merged.csv`
- `Id`, `ActivityHour`, `Calories`
- Hourly calorie expenditure and variation during the day 

### `hourlyIntensities_merged.csv`
- `Id`, `ActivityHour`, `TotalIntensity`, `AverageIntensity`
- When participants are most active and how this links to calories burnt.

Both datasets are on an hourly basis and can provide useful insight on a group dashboard when joined together


```{r}
dataset_summary <- tibble(
  Dataset = c("Daily Steps", "Hourly Calories",
              "Hourly Intensities"),
  Records = c(nrow(daily_steps),
              nrow(hourly_calories),
              nrow(hourly_intensities)),
  Participants = c(n_distinct(daily_steps$Id),
                   n_distinct(hourly_calories$Id),
                   n_distinct(hourly_intensities$Id))
)

dataset_summary
```
They also have the sam number of record so they can be accurately joined toeether

```{r shape}
# Number of rows and columns

dim(hourly_calories)
dim(hourly_intensities)

glimpse(daily_steps)
glimpse(hourly_calories)
glimpse(hourly_intensities)

n_distinct(daily_steps$Id)
n_distinct(hourly_calories$Id)
n_distinct(hourly_intensities$Id)
```
```{r}
colSums(is.na(daily_steps))
colSums(is.na(hourly_calories))
colSums(is.na(hourly_intensities))
```

```{r}
sum(duplicated(daily_steps))
sum(duplicated(hourly_calories))
```

No missing rows in any of these datasets or duplicates either. There a
```{r}
daily_steps %>%
  count(Id, ActivityDay) %>%
  filter(n > 1)

hourly_calories %>%
  count(Id, ActivityHour) %>%
  filter(n > 1)

hourly_intensities %>%
  count(Id, ActivityHour) %>%
  filter(n > 1)
```
Checking the date format: mm/dd/yyyy
```{r}
head(daily_steps$ActivityDay)
head(hourly_calories$ActivityHour)
head(hourly_intensities$ActivityHour)
```
Converting date formats so that they are standard
```{r}
daily_steps <- daily_steps %>%
  mutate(ActivityDay = mdy(ActivityDay))

hourly_calories <- hourly_calories %>%
  mutate(ActivityHour = mdy_hms(ActivityHour))

hourly_intensities <- hourly_intensities %>%
  mutate(ActivityHour = mdy_hms(ActivityHour))
```

Has the earliest and latest dates for both which are 04-12-2016 to 05-12-2016
```{r}
range(daily_steps$ActivityDay, na.rm = TRUE)
range(hourly_calories$ActivityHour, na.rm = TRUE)
range(hourly_intensities$ActivityHour, na.rm = TRUE)
```
```{r}
daily_steps %>%
  summarise(
    MeanSteps = mean(StepTotal, na.rm = TRUE),
    MedianSteps = median(StepTotal, na.rm = TRUE),
    MinSteps = min(StepTotal, na.rm = TRUE),
    MaxSteps = max(StepTotal, na.rm = TRUE),
    SDSteps = sd(StepTotal, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
summary(hourly_calories$Calories)

summary(hourly_intensities$TotalIntensity)

summary(hourly_intensities$AverageIntensity)
```
Absolutely insane steppers all these outliers lie on the the upper side 
```{r}
Q1 <- quantile(daily_steps$StepTotal, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
Q3 <- quantile(daily_steps$StepTotal, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)

IQR_steps <- Q3 - Q1

lower <- Q1 - 1.5 * IQR_steps
upper <- Q3 + 1.5 * IQR_steps

outliers <- daily_steps %>%
  filter(StepTotal < lower | StepTotal > upper)

outliers
```
## Joins
The possible joins would be between the calories and intensities files as these are both on an hourly basis and have the same number of rows 
```{r}
hourly_combined <- hourly_calories %>%
  inner_join(
    hourly_intensities,
    by = c("Id", "ActivityHour"),
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  )
hourly_combined
```
